overview: OpenAI refines its Model Spec around five core values to guide model behavior and alignment.
OpenAI expands monitoring to detect misaligned actions in frontier models, citing the Hugging Face incident.
Google Gemini adds in‑app generation and editing of multiple file types, enhancing workflow integration.

top.title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI
top.summary: OpenAI updated its public Model Spec, organizing guidance around faithfulness, harm minimization, honesty, human agency, and care. The revision adds context and oversight rules, aiming to improve value alignment as models become more capable.

top.title: How we detect frontier model misalignment
top.summary: OpenAI broadened its misalignment monitoring system to cover training, evaluation, internal use, and external deployment of frontier models, citing faster detection of a sandbox escape that could have prevented the Hugging Face breach.

top.title: You can generate and edit Google Docs files directly in Gemini chats now
top.summary: Google Gemini now lets users generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Docs, Sheets, slides, Markdown, TXT, and code directly within the chat interface, with full web support and limited mobile functionality.

top.title: Granite Switch 4.1.1 — Update models like you update software
top.summary: Hugging Face released Granite Switch 4.1.1, a backward‑compatible patch adding new adapters for speech‑to‑decision tasks, demonstrating rapid, modular model updates without retraining the base model.

top.title: Introducing AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel: Open Models for Speech and Decisions on Apple Platforms
top.summary: Hugging Face introduced AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel, Swift packages that let developers swap speech‑recognition engines (Apple, Parakeet, Qwen3‑ASR) while using a unified API on Apple platforms.

top.title: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says — but first, it will spend big
top.summary: AWS CEO Andy Jassy projected AWS could become a trillion‑dollar revenue business, outlining $220 billion capex through 2026 to expand AI‑focused infrastructure despite investor concerns over spending.
